en.title: Traditional music
en.summary: Folk, country, blues and the traditions behind popular music in English.

paragraphs: Much of the music enjoyed around the world today grew out of the traditions of ordinary people. In this lesson you will read about folk music, ballads and their American descendants, and you will practise asking about experience.

Traditional music was passed down by ear, from one singer to the next, long before it was written down. In Britain and Ireland, ballads told stories of love, war and travel, and many were collected in the early twentieth century. When emigrants crossed the Atlantic, they took their songs with them, and in the Appalachian Mountains these mixed with African-American styles to produce country music and the blues. Two friends are talking about a folk festival.

lines.speaker: Ada
lines.text: Have you ever been to a folk festival?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, last summer in Devon. The singers performed old ballads and the audience joined in the choruses.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Love, war and travel. Many of them were passed down by ear for centuries.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Fiddles, guitars, a banjo and some pipes. It was wonderful.

lines.speaker: Ada
lines.text: I've never been to one, but I'd love to go next year.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Then you should come with us.

paragraphs: **1. Have you ever...? asks about experience.** Use the present perfect without a time, and answer with a short answer or add a past simple detail. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
QuestionAnswer
Have you ever been to a festival?Yes, I have. / No, never.
Have you ever heard it?Yes, I heard it last summer.
How many times have you been?Twice.
I've never beenI've never been to one.

paragraphs: **2. The passive with a prepositional verb.** Pass down, write down and hand on keep their particle in the passive. See Introduction to Grammar: Voice.

blocks.html:
ActivePassive
People passed the songs down by ear.The songs were passed down by ear.
Collectors wrote the ballads down.The ballads were written down.
Singers hand them on.They are handed on from singer to singer.
Someone collected them.They were collected in the early 1900s.

items: Folk, country and blues grew from the traditions of ordinary people.
Jazz was born in New Orleans, and rock and roll developed from rhythm and blues.
Bagpipes are the national instrument of Scotland; the fiddle is common in folk music.
A chorus is the part of a song that is repeated.

paragraphs: The music of the British Isles and North America shaped each other through emigration over three centuries. Folk clubs, festivals and sessions in pubs keep the old songs alive, and many popular musicians still draw on them.
